evidence_quote: Genetic analysis identified a maternal hemizygous frameshift LAMP2 variant (NM_002294: c.973dupC, p. L325fs*).
Gene sequencing verified that the proband carried the mutation c.963G > A in the LAMP-2 gene.
note: Three-generation family; variant stated only for the proband; proband previously reported.

evidence_quote: The genetic analysis detected a pathogenic heterozygous mutation (c.973delC) in the LAMP2 gene, which confirmed a diagnosis of Danon disease.
note: Two male patients; literature Table S1 is referenced but not in the text.

evidence_quote: Genetic testing revealed an Xq24 microdeletion encompassing the entire LAMP2 gene.
note: Father and daughter; literature variant tables are supplementary (S1-S7) and not in the text.

evidence_quote: We report a case of DD in an adolescent male patient, confirmed by genetic testing.
note: Diagnosis confirmed by gene sequencing but no variant is reported.

evidence_quote: | Patient 1 (II-3) | c.928+3A>G/− | Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with hypertrophy of the left ventricle. Wolff–Parkinson–White syndrome. Second-grade hypertension. |
note: Two affected males plus two heterozygous mothers with cardiac findings (counted as 4).

evidence_quote: Nine patients carry the p.Arg293Ter variant, which is a germline pathogenic variant associated with Danon disease in the ClinVar database.
note: Two new Iranian family members plus a per-patient table of earlier carriers; one table row (USA, ref 8) is empty.

evidence_quote: The following whole-exome sequencing (WES) demonstrated a heterozygous variant in lysosome-associated membrane protein 2 (LAMP2) gene (c.696T>A; p.Cys232Ter)
The genetic test confirmed the presence of a mutation c.973dup;p (leu325profs25) in the LAMP-2 gene.
According to the results of DNA diagnostics, a diagnosis of Danon’s disease was confirmed: the same pathogenic mutation in a heterozygous state was detected in the LAMP2 gene as in her son.
note: Post-COVID myocarditis series of 10 cardiomyopathy patients; one has Danon disease (female patient K) and her deceased son is described briefly with a LAMP2 variant.

evidence_quote: Genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis of Danon disease with a LAMP2 c.733C > T (p.G245*) mutation (Figure 1M).
Currently, we have identified 22 different LAMP2 mutations in 26 families (Figure 3).
note: Narrative review; Japanese families summarized in aggregate and a mutation figure, no per-patient table.

evidence_quote: A hemizygous likely pathogenic variant was reported: LAMP2:c.645_651del (p.Lys215Asnfs25), resulting in diagnosis of Danon disease (DD).
The analysis included 116 patients with DD (of which 20% [n=23] were international) and was stratified by sex: female (n=64, 55%) and male (n=52, 45%) (Table 1).
note: Registry cohort reported in aggregate only.
